test_title: SSC MTS Previous Year Paper (Held on: 21 July 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: If a fundamental right of a citizen of India is violated, _____.

options.text: he has to appeal in the Supreme court only
he has to appeal in the district court first
he has the choice of either approaching the Supreme court directly or the High court
he has to appeal in the High court first

solution:
The correct answer is __**he has the choice of either approaching the Supreme court directly or the High court**__ . 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• If a fundamental right of a citizen of India is violated, he has the choice of either approaching the Supreme court directly or the High court.
 
• Provision for Laws Violating Fundamental Rights: Article 13 of the Indian constitution declares that all laws that are inconsistent with or in derogation of any of the fundamental rights shall be void.
 
• This power has been conferred on the Supreme Court (Article 32) and the high courts (Article 226).Further, the article declares that a constitutional amendment cannot be challenged (as it is not a law).
 
• The courts can issue various kinds of writs. These writs are habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto and certiorari. Dr. B. R. Ambedkar rightly declared Right to constitutional remedies as "the heart and soul" of Indian constitution. When a national or state emergency is declared, this right is suspended by the central government.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Constitution of India protects the Fundamental Rights of citizens of India.
 
• Fundamental rights are those rights that are essential for the intellectual, moral, and spiritual development of citizens of India.
 
• They are enshrined in **Articles 12-35 in Part III of the constitution**. It is a borrowed feature from the constitution of the USA.
 
• There are Six fundamentals rights recognized by the Indian constitution. 
 
 
• Right to Equality (Articles 14-18)
 
• Right to freedom (Articles 19-22)
 
• Right Against Exploitation (Articles 23-24)
 
• Right to freedom of Religion (Articles 25-28)
 
• Cultural and Educational Rights (Articles 29-30)
 
• Right to constitutional Remedies (Articles 32-35)​
